cue: How do you say something changed with no warning at all?

es.text: De la noche a la mañana
es.literal: from the night to the morning
es.example: El barrio se llenó de turistas de la noche a la mañana.
es.exampleTranslation: The neighbourhood filled up with tourists overnight.

it.literal: from the today to the tomorrow
it.example: Il quartiere si è riempito di turisti dall'oggi al domani.
it.exampleTranslation: The neighbourhood filled up with tourists overnight.

bridge.note: Both languages measure a sudden change by the shortest gap they can name, and they cut the gap in different places. Spanish crosses a night — from dark to light, with sleep in between, so the change happens while nobody is watching. Italian crosses a date — from today to tomorrow, with midnight in between, so the change happens because the calendar turned over. One is about not seeing it coming; the other is about how little time it took. Italian also does something Spanish does not: it puts articles on the bare adverbs, DALL'oggi AL domani, treating today and tomorrow as nouns you can travel between.

interference.es_to_it: Do not carry the night across: 'dalla notte alla mattina' is understood and is not the phrase. Italian goes day to day, and it needs the articles — oggi and domani are bare adverbs everywhere else, but here they take l' and al.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish will not travel from day to day here — 'del hoy al mañana' is not Spanish. It crosses the night instead, and takes no article on either noun beyond the ordinary la.

review.notes: PAIRING IS DICTIONARY-BACKED: PONS lists dall'oggi al domani against both 'de la noche a la mañana' and 'de un día para otro', and diccionarios.com gives the same. I chose the night version as the anchor because it is the more common and more vivid; 'de un día para otro' is the closer literal match and is the obvious alternate if a reviewer prefers it — note that choosing it would REMOVE the entry's whole bridge, since it crosses days exactly as the Italian does. ES REVIEWER, that is the decision.
